The numbers 1, 2, ..., 2100 are written on a board. Every second, Mark takes two numbers on the board, \( a \) and \( b \), erases them, and replaces them with \( \gcd(a, b) \) and \( \operatorname{lcm}(a, b) \). Mark stops once any move he makes will not change the numbers written on the board. Compute the number of divisors of the 2026th smallest positive integer written on the board when he finishes.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

Let \(N=2100\). For a prime \(p\), write \(v_p(n)\) for the exponent of \(p\) in \(n\).

A move on \(a,b\) replaces \(v_p(a),v_p(b)\) by
\[
\min(v_p(a),v_p(b)),\quad \max(v_p(a),v_p(b)).
\]
So for each prime \(p\), the multiset of \(p\)-adic exponents on the board is invariant.

Mark stops exactly when every pair of numbers on the board is comparable by divisibility. Thus the final numbers can be ordered as
\[
x_1\mid x_2\mid \cdots \mid x_{2100}.
\]
For each prime \(p\), the sequence \(v_p(x_1),v_p(x_2),\dots,v_p(x_{2100})\) is nondecreasing and has the same multiset as the initial exponents among \(1,2,\dots,2100\). Therefore \(v_p(x_i)\) is the \(i\)-th smallest \(p\)-adic exponent among the numbers \(1,\dots,2100\).

We need \(x_{2026}\). Among \(2100\) exponents, the \(2026\)-th smallest is the
\[
2100-2026+1=75
\]
th largest.

For a prime \(p\), the 75th largest exponent is at least \(k\) iff at least \(75\) of the numbers \(1,\dots,2100\) are divisible by \(p^k\), i.e.
\[
\left\lfloor \frac{2100}{p^k}\right\rfloor \ge 75.
\]
Since \(2100=75\cdot 28\), this is equivalent to
\[
p^k\le 28.
\]
So the required exponent of \(p\) is the largest \(k\) such that \(p^k\le 28\).

Thus:
\[
v_2=4,\quad v_3=3,\quad v_5=2,
\]
and for the primes \(7,11,13,17,19,23\), the exponent is \(1\). All larger primes have exponent \(0\).

Hence the 2026th smallest final number is
\[
2^4\cdot 3^3\cdot 5^2\cdot 7\cdot 11\cdot 13\cdot 17\cdot 19\cdot 23,
\]
which is \(\operatorname{lcm}(1,2,\dots,28)\).

Its number of positive divisors is
\[
(4+1)(3+1)(2+1)(1+1)^6
=5\cdot 4\cdot 3\cdot 64
=3840.
\]

\[
\boxed{3840}
\]
